A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SupCLAP work and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Existing content can be reliably matched across the expanded and renumbered appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval, zero-shot classification, ablation, trajectory-drift, semantic-radius and computational-overhead results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds repeated-run statistics, transfer evaluations, new comparisons and robustness analyses.

M1.justification: The support-vector construction, SVR loss, static and dynamic radius modeling, constraint term and inference procedure are retained. Applying the existing regularizer to ATRI-CACL adds an evaluation without introducing a new SVR component.

E1.justification: Appendix E.2 adds WavCaps training and evaluation, plus AudioCaps-to-Clotho and Clotho-to-AudioCaps transfer scenarios. This substantially broadens coverage beyond the retained within-dataset retrieval, multilingual retrieval and classification evaluations.

E2.justification: v2 adds Cacophony to Table 1, a Simple Reweight control in Appendix E.4, and ATRI-CACL with SVR variants in the multilingual comparison. Table 2 drops the separately reported Elizalde et al. (2023) row; most other changes from author names to model names preserve existing comparators.

E3.justification: New protocols include a 5,000-sample WavCaps test holdout, cross-dataset transfer, random initialization of both encoders with text-encoder depth reduced from 24 to 12 layers, and selecting 6, 12 or 18 hard negatives from 720 candidates. The original main training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds distribution-shift tests, positive-pair similarity distributions, a gradient-reweighting control, convergence curves, weak-encoder robustness tests and hard-negative sensitivity analysis. These investigate generalization and the proposed mechanism beyond v1's retained component, batch-size, weight and radius analyses.

E5.justification: v1 reports retrieval point estimates without seed counts or uncertainty. Appendix E.1 and Table 4 first report five independent random-seed runs and means with standard deviations. The accompanying significance claim refers to confidence intervals, although no interval construction or formal test is specified.

E6.justification: Existing SupCLAP headline scores and retained ablation and overhead values are unchanged. v2 adds seed aggregates, comparator entries, WavCaps, transfer, reweighting and weak-encoder results, plus new plotted findings. For example, Table 5 newly reports DynamicSVR WavCaps R@1 of 21.30 for A2T and 8.30 for T2A; these are additional results, not improvements over a v1 WavCaps experiment.

T1.justification: New Appendix C.1 derives the one-step change in squared positive-pair distance, isolating the perpendicular component's eta-squared norm term as a penalty. This adds a formal connection between drift and alignment progress. The original SVR Jacobian and force-decomposition derivation is retained in Appendix D.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list now explicitly claim no additional training data or inference computation, refining v1's general negligible-overhead claim. The central trajectory-drift, SVR, radius-modeling and performance contributions retain their scope.

C2.justification: v1 explains declining radius through preserving hard-negative information later in training. v2 links it to decreasing negative-pair similarity and argues that harder batches require larger radii (Appendix E.8). It also adds substantive interpretations of transfer, noisy-encoder robustness and why SVR differs from scalar gradient reweighting.

D1.justification: v2 supplies implementation information for added experiments, including reproducing ATRI's CACL objective, scaling P+ with a learnable scalar for Simple Reweight, and the hard-negative sampling procedure. Core SVR hyperparameters, optimizer, hardware and inference details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A's related-work discussion is retained. v2 newly emphasizes compatibility with ATRI-CACL, which was already cited, and removes bibliography entries for Deshmukh et al. (2022), Mei et al. (2022) and Oncescu et al. (2021), while retaining corresponding model-level comparison rows.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order remain intact. v2 shortens the conclusion and Figure 1 caption, revises the radius interpretation, changes baseline naming, adds the conference header and reorganizes appendix numbering around the new material.

P2.justification: v2 adds five tables and Figures 4–7, including a four-panel convergence display. It expands the multilingual table, changes comparator rows and labels in the main tables, enlarges Figure 2 and relocates retained appendix displays. Figures 1–3 retain their underlying graphics.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for repeatability, transfer and predictor robustness through five-seed reporting, cross-dataset tests and targeted mechanism analyses—important gaps in v1's support for SVR. The added one-step derivation also clarifies the alignment argument. These gains outweigh the statistical overstatement in Appendix E.1, where standard-deviation ranges are discussed as confidence intervals. Test-set checkpoint selection in Section 4.1.2 remains an unresolved limitation.
